For $u=(u_x,u_y,u_z)$ and $v=(v_x,v_y,v_z)$ in $\mathbb R^3$, define $u\times v=(u_yv_z-u_zv_y,\,u_zv_x-u_xv_z,\,u_xv_y-u_yv_x)$.

derivations.claim: The standard horizontal-square parametrization has upward area vector and flux one for the vertical field.
Swapping parameters reverses the area vector and gives flux minus one.
The unequal values refute parametrization independence without an orientation condition.

boundaries.reason: The unit square is nonempty.

boundaries.evidence: The horizontal field components and area-vector components are zero and retained in both dot products.
The two flux values are exactly one and minus one.
Both parametrizations are regular, so the sign change is not caused by a rank failure.
The swap maps every edge and corner of the closed square to the corresponding boundary.

boundaries.reason: The witness maps and field are explicit.
A false universal assertion is refuted by one witness.
No equivalence is asserted.
